answer: A newcomer earns a seat by commissioning a load test on a ferrous bridge: a calibrated weight hangs from one named vertex of the span above a mesa gorge, and two engineers measure the deflection the same day. A reading off by more than a millimetre, or a late log, voids the claim and burns a 550 POA bond. Each test costs a $260 rigging fee plus a $90 engineer fee, so 100 fakes need 100 tests, $35,000 in fees and 55,000 POA in bonds, while honest builders prove real spans carry real weight.
